subject.title: fix(shared): cap backtick delimiter length to prevent unbounded repeat

question: Should oversized code payloads remain losslessly representable, or should OpenClaw reject or truncate them at an explicit caller boundary before Markdown formatting?
rationale: A bounded delimiter cannot represent every arbitrary input while preserving the current containment contract, so the acceptable oversized-input behavior must be chosen rather than inferred by automation.

options.title: Limit input before formatting
options.body: Keep the shared formatter lossless and reject or truncate oversized payloads at a named caller boundary with visible behavior and focused tests.

options.title: Define a lossy formatter contract
options.body: Permit truncation or transformation inside these helpers, but document the changed API behavior and prove callers cannot mistake transformed content for the original.

options.title: Retain proportional delimiters
options.body: Keep exact current formatting and accept output growth while investigating whether real callers already enforce adequate payload limits.

recommendation.title: Limit input before formatting
recommendation.body: Keep the shared formatter lossless and reject or truncate oversized payloads at a named caller boundary with visible behavior and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes a shared formatting and hostile-input contract, making the repository-wide shared-core owner the best available decision route.
